title: Directional derivatives of weighted forms
statement:
Let $I$ be finite, let $w:I	o br$, let $p>1$ and $rho
ein br$, and let $g,h:I	o br$ with $g_i
earrow0$ for every $i$. Define $G(f)=sum_iw_i|f_i|^p$ and $F(f)=rho^2sum_iw_if_i^2+(1-rho^2)(sum_iw_if_i)^2$. At $t=0$, the derivative of $G(g+th)$ is $psum_iw_ig_i^{p-1}h_i$, and the derivative of $F(g+th)$ is $2\bigl(\rho^2\sum_iw_ig_ih_i+(1-\rho^2)(\sum_iw_ig_i)(\sum_iw_ih_i)\bigr)$.
replaced: Let $I$ be finite, $w:I\to\bbr$, $p>1$, $\rho\in\bbr$, $g_i\ge0$, and $h\in\bbr^I$. Define $G(f)=\sum_iw_i|f_i|^p$ and $F(f)=\rho^2\sum_iw_if_i^2+(1-\rho^2)(\sum_iw_if_i)^2$. At $t=0$, the derivative of $G(g+th)$ is $p\sum_iw_ig_i^{p-1}h_i$, and that of $F(g+th)$ is $2[\rho^2\sum_iw_ig_ih_i+(1-\rho^2)(\sum_iw_ig_i)(\sum_iw_ih_i)]$.
